selection.status: All 21 raw AAI v5.0.1 frontier configurations in the supplied four-provider Standard comparison; task-fit exceptions are separate. Not a live API or account-access test.

LM.description: Candidate for trivial, tightly bounded work with inexpensive acceptance checks.

L.description: Retained Luna Max profile for explicit selection or custom pools, not a synonym for Luna Medium.

TL.description: Use for small, specified changes, source transformations, or straightforward visual interpretation following an established pattern, with inexpensive checks. Prefer another eligible profile when substantial interpretation or reframing is needed.

TM.description: Execute established implementation or screen-based workflows and structure source-rich writing, including substantial multi-step work. Supply relevant patterns, decision boundaries, and acceptance checks, and surface unresolved choices instead of narrowing the task.

TH.description: Handle harder bounded diagnosis, implementation, synthesis, or visual analysis with explicit ownership and checks. Ask the coordinator to reframe unresolved problems rather than assuming more Terra effort will resolve them.

SL.description: Candidate for routine bounded work with clear acceptance checks.

SM.description: General implementation, analysis, debugging, and verification candidate at Medium effort.

SH.description: General implementation, analysis, debugging, and verification candidate at High effort. Additional effort is a routing choice, not a proven task-specific advantage.

SX.description: General implementation, analysis, debugging, and verification candidate at XHigh effort. Choose it when the assignment justifies testing additional reasoning.

SMAX.description: General implementation, analysis, debugging, and verification candidate at Max effort. Max does not imply review-only work or guaranteed improvement.

AL.description: General reasoning, implementation, and analysis candidate at Low effort. Browser work requires verified tools, not an Astra-specific assignment.

AM.description: Retained Astra Medium profile for explicit selection or custom pools.

AH.description: General reasoning, implementation, debugging, and analysis candidate at High effort. No browser-only specialization is implied.

AX.description: General reasoning, implementation, and analysis candidate at XHigh effort. Compare checked results rather than assuming a distinct task specialty.

AMAX.description: General reasoning, implementation, and verification candidate at Max effort. Particular modes may assign independent review, without limiting the model to that role.

HMED.description: Candidate for small, well-scoped worker assignments with concrete checks.

HH.description: Candidate for bounded delegation when additional Haiku reasoning may reduce controller repair work.

HM.description: Bounded Haiku XHigh worker candidate, also used by the optional Opus/Haiku preset.

HK.description: Retained Haiku XHigh profile with a soft 100K context target, not an independently enforced cap.

HMAX.description: Candidate for bounded delegation where higher Haiku reasoning is worth testing against accepted-task throughput.

SNH.description: Middle-pool candidate for work needing stronger judgment than a bounded Haiku assignment.

SNX.description: Exact retained Sonnet XHigh option for economical knowledge-work comparison.

OM.description: General-purpose implementation and integration candidate in Claude-primary pools.

OH.description: General implementation, analysis, and independent review candidate. Separate frontend preference evidence supports a targeted trial, not exclusive eligibility.

OX.description: General implementation, architecture, debugging, and independent review candidate at XHigh effort.

OMAX.description: Candidate for demanding Claude-primary work or a justified Codex-primary Performance escalation.

FM.description: Selective candidate for open-ended reasoning, architecture, implementation, and review at Medium effort.

FH.description: Preferred Fable trial for demanding reasoning, architecture, implementation, or independent review. The work order determines authorship and delegation authority.

FX.description: Optional XHigh comparison for demanding reasoning, implementation, or review. Higher effort is not a demonstrated universal advantage over High.

FMAX.description: Exceptional on-call comparison for demanding reasoning, implementation, or review when the expected benefit warrants its cost.

MFH.description: Investigate repository structure, existing fixes, and root causes using source evidence. Default to diagnosis and focused checks. Implement when the work order authorizes edits.

MFX.description: Examine cross-system failures with competing hypotheses and challenge a proposed plan against evidence. Default to discriminating checks, not a second dispatcher. Implement when the work order authorizes edits.

LL.description: Trivial extraction and mechanical edits with cheap checks.

HL.description: Cheap bounded work with explicit inputs and inexpensive checks.

EX.description: Bounded reasoning candidate when an exact Muse adapter is verified.

EMAX.description: Higher-effort Ember candidate for checked comparison.

GCM.description: General reasoning candidate with verified Gemini tools and account access.

GCH.description: General reasoning candidate with verified Gemini tools and account access.

MFMAX.description: Orchestration and steerable-prose preference trial through a verified Muse Code subscription adapter.
MFMAX.label: Muse Wonder Full

KK31.description: Terminal-engineering candidate. Choose an explicit supported runtime effort before dispatch.

GA4H.specialty: Visual reasoning and MCP tool use

DSFH.description: Budget workflow-automation experiment. Rolling alias currently maps to V4.1 Flash 1017.

GLMMAX.specialty: Writing preference and private hosting trials

MSMAX.description: Reviewed professional-document trial. Professional-reasoning evidence does not specify effort.

CYBER.description: Restricted authorized-security candidate. No runtime effort is pinned.

ui-pro.fit: Capture screenshots and run interaction, keyboard, and focus checks with verified browser/computer-control tools. Record build, route, viewport, theme, and state.
Diagnose concrete defects in baseline and intermediate screenshots. Return unresolved framing to the coordinator; this critique does not replace the final council.
Own focused UI implementation in the project's existing design system and idioms.
Own substantial scoped UI implementation or refactoring across related components.
Review the final candidate independently against the requirements, rubric, and functional evidence. Fresh intermediate reviews are also eligible.
Critique visual design, interaction, and rendering code from a separate model's perspective. Fresh intermediate reviews are also eligible.
Critique the candidate against existing components, tokens, and repository patterns. Fresh intermediate reviews are also eligible.

browser-3d.fit: Implement conventional UI, interactions, asset manifests, automation, and tests. Also handle routine browser journeys and screenshot collection with verified tool access.
Build scene-generation and export pipelines, browser rendering, and asset integration. Diagnose performance problems while preserving the approved visual direction.
Resolve difficult rendering, shader, transform, collision, or integration failures with interacting constraints. Return demonstrated causes and verified corrections.
Handle exceptional engineering problems or independently review a complex candidate against functional and performance requirements. Use a fresh reviewer when this profile authored the work.

Create and refine geometry, materials, lighting, and spatial composition through the available 3D toolchain. Inspect actual browser output for visual fidelity and interaction defects, separately from authored work when reviewing.

council.fit: Develop a decision proposal, test its assumptions, and compare concrete implementation tradeoffs.
Challenge architectural choices against requirements, source evidence, and simpler alternatives.
Investigate competing hypotheses and identify evidence that distinguishes proposed approaches.
Add an optional fourth perspective on assumptions, alternatives, and decision criteria.
Advise on requirements and overlooked constraints, challenging the premise when useful and proposing materially distinct alternatives. This advisory slot adds no vote.

codex-burn.fit: Consider for general analysis or implementation at Low effort. Browser assignments require verified tools and session access. Select only authorized backlog work.
Use for ordinary authorized implementation or verification with a clear change surface and acceptance checks.
Use for backlog diagnosis or integration where uncertainty warrants additional reasoning.
Use for difficult authorized implementation or debugging with multiple interacting constraints.
Consider for demanding reasoning, implementation, debugging, or analysis. High effort does not imply a browser specialty. Select only authorized backlog work.
Consider for demanding analysis, implementation, or verification when task fit warrants Max effort. Verify tools for interactive work. Select only authorized backlog work.

claude-burn.fit: Use for a bounded one-off backlog packet with concrete inputs, ownership, and acceptance checks.
Use for scoped authorized implementation or analysis needing more judgment than a small Haiku packet.
Use for general-purpose authorized implementation and integration spanning related files.
Use for uncertain backlog implementation or debugging where additional reasoning is justified.
Use for difficult authorized analysis, implementation, or integration with interacting requirements.
Use for demanding authorized work when sustained reasoning fits the backlog, not merely to consume allowance.

amusing.fit: Implement bounded changes in the repository's existing idioms. Prefer the smallest complete change and inexpensive acceptance checks.
Debug difficult invariants or integrate changes with interacting constraints. Require evidence that the fix addresses the cause without expanding scope.
Prefer for substantial scoped implementation or refactoring when the task fits Opus Medium. Medium is not a universal optimum, so compare the actual candidate and checks.
Independently review maintainability and architecture against the repository's existing design. Propose concrete simpler alternatives where they preserve the required behavior.

Independently test functional behavior, failure cases, and implementation assumptions against the requirements. Report evidence and maintainability concerns without claiming model-specific code-quality authority.

Consider for demanding implementation or a fresh framing when the current approach overcomplicates the task or offers too-similar alternatives. Preserve acceptance criteria and distinguish authorship from independent review.
Investigate repository structure, existing fixes, and root causes using source evidence. Default to diagnosis and focused checks. Implement when the work order authorizes edits.

Examine cross-system failures with competing hypotheses and challenge a proposed plan against evidence. Default to discriminating checks, not a second dispatcher. Implement when the work order authorizes edits.

reviewer.prompt: Review the assigned work and return evidence and uncertainties. Honor the requested role, authorized checks, file ownership, and any shared deadline. Available tools do not authorize unrelated edits.

muse:muse_code_subscription.verification_scope: Existing Muse Code adapter route only. Current account access, model entitlement, tools, and effective effort require dispatch preflight.
